plans.note: Section 9 is the express limitation of liability; check mutuality, cap size and whether indemnity (sec-8-2), confidentiality (sec-10) and IP breaches are carved out. Section 8's disclaimer may interact with the cap.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's third-party IP indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify defence obligation, procedure, and that any Corio-side indemnity is narrow and not uncapped under sec-9.

Grant of Rights plus the defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY are the likely vehicles for field-of-use or competing-product restrictions on us; also scan Shared Resources and Miscellaneous for residual covenants.

Check Grant of Rights and Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation) for any obligation that Corio host or promote only Commerce One procurement software or refrain from sourcing competing applications.

Pricing/Exhibit B, revenue sharing and payment terms are where a most-favoured-pricing clause would sit; confirm direction — an MFN running to Commerce One (best terms from us) is the concern, one in Corio's favour is fine.
No dedicated hiring clause in the outline; if present it would be buried in Miscellaneous, Confidentiality or Shared Resources (RELATIONSHIP MANAGERS). Confirm absence before reporting missing.

Section 11 (Term and Termination) governs; test whether Corio has convenience termination on notice without penalty and whether Commerce One can terminate mid-term or on payment/fee grounds referenced in sec-4.
Initial term, auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window sit in Section 11; renewal pricing uplift, if any, would appear in Exhibit B pricing.
Miscellaneous should contain governing law, venue and any dispute resolution; the defined term RULES suggests an arbitration reference to check for foreign or mandatory arbitration.
Assignment/change-of-control clause expected in Miscellaneous; confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One cannot terminate on a Corio change of control.

Ownership language should appear in Grant of Rights and the DEVELOPMENTS / EMPLOYEE NDA-INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions; verify Corio retains its own IP, customer data and hosting configurations, with trademark use limited under sec-6.

Section 2 Grant of Rights plus Exhibit A software list define scope; check it is non-revocable at will, covers hosting for CUSTOMERS/SOFTWARE USERS, affiliates and contractors, and that DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE limits are workable.
Any records inspection tied to revenue-sharing or user-count reporting would sit in Fees or Exhibit B payment terms; test notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost.
Look for late-payment interest, penalties or shortfall payments in Fees/Payment Terms and any support-related penalties in Exhibit C; service credits flowing to us are acceptable.
Section 7 Warranties and Disclaimer, read with the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions and the maintenance obligations in Section 5; assess duration, remedy and breadth of the disclaimer.
No insurance heading in the outline; check Miscellaneous and the indemnification section for any coverage undertaking before concluding it is missing.

Fees, Exhibit B pricing and the revenue-sharing schedule are the likely home of minimum guarantees, seat minimums or take-or-pay commitments; verify any minimum has an exit or is tied to actual usage.

Effects-of-termination language in Section 11 plus the Section 12 source code escrow are the relevant hooks; check for wind-down/run-off rights for existing CUSTOMERS and return or continued access to data and software.
